independent_replay: Stage0 and stage1 archives were extracted separately. The old location pair in stage1 revision-1 matched the prior stage0 current pair byte for byte; all three grid outputs were unchanged. An examiner-only standard-library eight-corner calculation from stage0 grid CSV checked six row classifications and 48 real/imag components, with maximum absolute difference 4.55e-13. From stage1 archive, the bundled dev5 wheel was installed in a fresh venv and imported from that venv's site-packages. The ordinary entrypoint ran twice with exit 0, 20 run checks and nine project tests passed, and all 16 output files retained their hashes and modification times. A separate extraction changed one coordinate at the same request path without a model turn; the ordinary entrypoint created revision-2 with the previous current table bytes, left revision-1 intact, and a repeat changed no files. The venv used --system-site-packages.
limitations: The solver session was fresh, but it inherited the previously reviewer-repaired project, including its artifact-history structure. This is not unassisted greenfield creation or evidence that the prior repair was autonomous.

The project archived exact prior output bytes but did not retain the pre-correction same-path request JSON bytes. That source is held only in the examiner evidence and the inherited archive; project-native historical input-byte provenance remains incomplete.
The second correction was an independent command-level probe of the delivered project, not a second natural-language Agent continuation.
Examiner-private materials were not protected by operating-system read permissions, so this was staged disclosure, not strict blind isolation.
The synthetic local dielectric-response calculation has no RF wave or field solution and does not identify deposited power or an absorption location.
The replay venv used system site packages, so this does not prove offline dependency reinstallation.
